title: Basis of the Subscription and Seat Licence Charge — Corporate Travel Programmes
content:
The subscription is charged in advance for each billing period at the tier's monthly rate, or at its annual rate where the company is invoiced yearly; the two are never both charged. This is the charging basis for the Corporate Travel Programmes, and it governs what a billing period costs the company before any booking is made.

## Seats beyond those included

Seats beyond those included in the tier are charged at the tier's seat licence rate for each seat for each month of the period, counted on the seats contracted rather than the seats actually assigned.

The chargeable quantity is therefore the seats contracted less the seats the tier's subscription already carries, taken as nil where the seats contracted do not exceed the seats included. The seat licence charge for a month is that chargeable quantity multiplied by the tier's seat licence rate for each seat for each month.

## Part months

A period that begins or ends part way through a month is charged pro rata by whole days out of the days in that month. The proration basis is whole days out of the days in the month: the days charged are counted whole, and the denominator is the number of days the month itself has.

## Worked illustration on hypothetical inputs

Take a hypothetical company on the Business Pro Programme, whose subscription carries 35 traveller seats and whose seat licence rate is 6.00 for each seat for each month, and suppose it has contracted 60 traveller seats and is invoiced monthly.

- Chargeable seats: 60 seats contracted less 35 seats carried by the subscription gives 25 seats.
- Seat licence charge for a full month: 25 multiplied by 6.00 gives 150.00.
- Subscription for that month: the tier's monthly rate, charged in advance, and its annual rate not charged at all.

Suppose instead that this company's period runs from the sixteenth day of a month of 30 days to the end of that month. The charge for that part month is prorated by 15 whole days out of the 30 days in that month.

## Notes on the basis

- The count that matters for the seat licence charge is the seats contracted. A company that contracts 60 seats and has assigned only 20 of them to named travellers is still charged on 60.
- Where the seats contracted do not exceed the seats the tier's subscription carries, the chargeable quantity is nil and no seat licence charge arises for that month.
- The monthly rate and the annual rate are alternatives set by how the company is invoiced, never two charges on one period.
